GS.rationale: Goldman Sachs exhibits genuine fundamental strength: Q1 2026 revenue +14.4% YoY to $17.23B, EPS +24.3% to $17.55, operating margin 37.7%, and ROE improving from 12.0% to 14.7%. The franchise is elite (#1 global equities, premier advisory), and the strategic pivot back to institutional strengths is well-timed with a recovering capital markets cycle. Q2 2026 results (reported ~July 14) showed accelerating revenue to $20.24B with a 7.4% stock surge, and multiple analyst upgrades (HSBC, Jefferies, Wells Fargo) with targets up to $1,325. However, the stock has already re-rated significantly: trailing P/E at 18.32x is at the 74th percentile of its 365-day range, P/B at 2.70x is at the 81st percentile, and the stock is up ~55% from its Oct 2025 low. The market has priced in much of the earnings improvement. The forward P/E of ~13.8x on HSBC's 2027 estimate offers some runway, but the trailing valuation leaves limited margin of safety. Leverage has increased to 16.8x (from 14.5x), and a flattening yield curve (10Y-2Y spread at 0.34%) plus hawkish Fed signals are modest headwinds. The Q2 beat and analyst upgrades provide a near-term positive catalyst (pillar 3), but the already-elevated trailing valuation caps the score. Mildly attractive: strong franchise and momentum, but priced in.
